\chapter{Grandparents and Family: Two New Signs}
\label{ch:mw-family-seven}
\hlchaptermodality{11}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can add paternal grandfather, paternal grandmother, and family to the earlier four-word map while keeping regional and household variation explicit.}

Three more family labels secured by ear before writing, with only \mw{द} and \mw{व} added one sign at a time before the seven-word map.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[dādā]{Hear \emph{dādā} — paternal grandfather}

\label{lesson:MW-C08-hear-dada}



\begin{quote}
Recall the four-word family checkpoint, say the known word for name, then write familiar \textbf{\mw{ठ}} once.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\emph{dādā} — \textbf{paternal grandfather}
\end{quote}

Hear the same long beat twice: \emph{dā-dā}. Say it once. This chapter follows the source's \emph{dādā} form; other documented Marwari materials also record \emph{dādo}. That variation is real and is not an error to erase. Writing waits one step.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Choose among brother, sister, and paternal grandfather from three heard words. Repeat only \emph{dādā}.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Say \emph{dā-dā} once, then stop.

Sources: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-4-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 4} and \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/d-glossary-of-rajasthani-language}{Marwari Pathshala, D glossary}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[da]{\mw{द} — one sign for both beats}

\label{lesson:MW-W08-da}



\begin{quote}
Write brother, then the known wellbeing answer. Say paternal grandfather and sister; keep \emph{dādā} oral until the new sign appears.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script — one sign}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mw{द}} — \emph{da}
\end{quote}

Keep the model visible. Trace the curved lower body, return to the upright, and add the headline. Say \emph{da} after the pen stops.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Copy \textbf{\mw{द}} once. Cover it, wait five seconds, and write it twice with a small space: \textbf{\mw{द} \mw{द}}. Say \emph{dā-dā} without assembling the word yet.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Read \textbf{\mw{द}} once, then stop.

Source: \href{https://www.unicode.org/charts/PDF/U0900.pdf}{Unicode Devanagari chart}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[dādā]{\mw{दादा} — the repeated word}

\label{lesson:MW-C08-dada}



\begin{quote}
Ask and answer wellbeing once. Write \textbf{\mw{द}} and familiar \textbf{\mw{ा}}, then say sister from memory.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mw{दा}} + \textbf{\mw{दा}} $\to$ \textbf{\mw{दादा}} — \emph{dādā} — paternal grandfather
\end{quote}

The spelling repeats exactly what the ear heard: two matching long beats.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Look at \textbf{\mw{दादा}}, cover it, wait five seconds, and write it once. Point to both copies of \textbf{\mw{ा}} before reading the whole word.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Read \textbf{\mw{दादा}} once, then stop.

Sources: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-4-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 4} and \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/d-glossary-of-rajasthani-language}{Marwari Pathshala, D glossary}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[dādī]{Hear \emph{dādī} — paternal grandmother}

\label{lesson:MW-C08-hear-dadi}



\begin{quote}
Say and write paternal grandfather and sister, then give the known see-you-later line and its two meaning parts.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\emph{dādī} — \textbf{paternal grandmother}
\end{quote}

The first beat matches \emph{dādā}. The last vowel changes: \emph{dā-dī}. Hear the pair \emph{dādā — dādī}, then say only \emph{dādī}.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Hear either \emph{dādā} or \emph{dādī}. Identify paternal grandfather or paternal grandmother before repeating the word.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Say \emph{dādā — dādī} once, then stop.

Sources: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-4-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 4} and \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/d-glossary-of-rajasthani-language}{Marwari Pathshala, D glossary}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[dādī]{\mw{दादी} — change the final vowel}

\label{lesson:MW-C08-dadi}



\begin{quote}
Recall the four-word family checkpoint, write \textbf{\mw{छ}}, then write \textbf{\mw{दा}} and \textbf{\mw{दी}}. Say sister once.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mw{दा}} + \textbf{\mw{दी}} $\to$ \textbf{\mw{दादी}} — \emph{dādī} — paternal grandmother
\end{quote}

Compare \textbf{\mw{दादा}} and \textbf{\mw{दादी}}. Only the final vowel sign changes.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Hear \emph{dādā} or \emph{dādī}. Write the matching word without a model, then check the final vowel sign.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Read \textbf{\mw{दादा} — \mw{दादी}} once, then stop.

Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-4-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 4}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[parivār]{Hear \emph{parivār} — family}

\label{lesson:MW-C08-hear-parivaar}



\begin{quote}
Say paternal grandfather and sister, write paternal grandmother, then write \textbf{\mw{े}} once.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\emph{parivār} — \textbf{family}
\end{quote}

Hear three small groups: \emph{pa-ri-vār}. Say them smoothly once. The word names a family group; it does not require every family to have the same members.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Hear one group word and two relation words. Identify \emph{parivār} as family, then say it once from the meaning alone.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Say \emph{parivār} once, then stop.

Sources: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-4-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 4} and \href{https://nepal.sil.org/resources/archives/63768}{SIL International, Marwari–English Dictionary archive}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[va]{\mw{व} — the middle of family}

\label{lesson:MW-W08-va}



\begin{quote}
Say family and paternal grandmother. Write \textbf{\mw{द}} and \textbf{\mw{ि}} once.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script — one sign}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mw{व}} — \emph{va}
\end{quote}

Keep the model visible. Trace the rounded lower body, rise to the upright, and finish with the headline. Say \emph{va} after the hand stops.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Copy \textbf{\mw{व}} once. Cover it, wait five seconds, and write it once. Say the middle sound group \emph{vār} from \emph{parivār}.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Read \textbf{\mw{व}} once, then stop.

Source: \href{https://www.unicode.org/charts/PDF/U0900.pdf}{Unicode Devanagari chart}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[parivār]{\mw{परिवार} — family on the page}

\label{lesson:MW-C08-parivaar}



\begin{quote}
Write \textbf{\mw{प}}, \textbf{\mw{रि}}, \textbf{\mw{व}}, and \textbf{\mw{ार}} as four small units. Write paternal grandfather and \textbf{\mw{ल}}, then say paternal grandmother.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mw{प}} + \textbf{\mw{रि}} + \textbf{\mw{वा}} + \textbf{\mw{र}} $\to$ \textbf{\mw{परिवार}} — \emph{parivār} — family
\end{quote}

Remember that \textbf{\mw{ि}} is written before \textbf{\mw{र}} but read after it: \emph{ri}.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Look at \textbf{\mw{परिवार}}, cover it, wait eight seconds, and write the four chunks. Uncover and check \textbf{\mw{रि}} and \textbf{\mw{व}} separately.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Read \textbf{\mw{परिवार}} once without romanization.

Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-4-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 4}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[Practice]{Retrieve three family words}

\label{lesson:MW-R08-family-foundation}



\begin{quote}
Say and write family, then write \textbf{\mw{ब}} and the known \textbf{\mw{पाछे} \mw{मिलसू}} once.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
1. \textbf{Listen:} identify \emph{mā̃}, \emph{bāp}, or \emph{dādī} from sound alone. 2. \textbf{Speak:} say the word from one relation cue. 3. \textbf{Read:} match \textbf{\mw{मां}}, \textbf{\mw{बाप}}, and \textbf{\mw{दादी}} to their meanings. 4. \textbf{Write:} write one heard word without a model.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Stop after one accurate pass.

Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-4-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 4}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[Practice]{Build the seven-word family map}

\label{lesson:MW-R08-family-map}



\begin{quote}
Say and write paternal grandmother, then complete the earlier four-skill see-you-later response once.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Place four cards under the correct cues: \textbf{\mw{भाई}}, \textbf{\mw{बहन}}, \textbf{\mw{दादा}}, and \textbf{\mw{परिवार}}. Read each card, turn it over, and write only the one named aloud.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Stop after one accurate map.

Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-4-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 4}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[Practice]{Payoff — seven family labels in four skills}

\label{lesson:MW-C08-family-seven}



\begin{quote}
Read the seven-word line once. Cover it before the scored pass.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mw{मां} — \mw{बाप} — \mw{भाई} — \mw{बहन} — \mw{दादा} — \mw{दादी} — \mw{परिवार}}
\end{quote}

These are labels for understanding and describing relationships, not a required family structure. Regional and household choices remain valid when documented.

\subsection*{Your turn}
1. \textbf{Listen:} identify four randomly heard labels. 2. \textbf{Speak:} produce four different labels from relation cues. 3. \textbf{Read:} match all seven printed words to meanings. 4. \textbf{Write:} write three heard labels without a model.

Score all four skills separately. A perfect spoken map does not replace missing reading or writing.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Stop after one independently accurate pass.

Sources: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-4-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 4}, \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/d-glossary-of-rajasthani-language}{Marwari Pathshala, D glossary}, and \href{https://nepal.sil.org/resources/archives/63768}{SIL International, Marwari–English Dictionary archive}.
\end{tcolorbox}
